entries.name: Fox squirrel
behaviour: caches nuts and relies on memory or luck to find them again
dives from branches into a flashy driving dodge when a hawk passes
dens high in mature hardwoods, often a used woodpecker or squirrel hollow

voxel_model.pattern: rusty-red flanks and tail with a black head, orange-brown

entries.notes: The bigger cousin of the eastern gray squirrel in the southern US; fond of farms and oak groves.

entries.name: Common gray fox
behaviour: the only American fox that climbs trees, using retractable hooked claws
sleeps in forks of oak and pine branches
more frugivorous than other canids - eastern persimmon and blackberry matter

voxel_model.pattern: salt-and-pepper grey back, rusty sides, black tail ridge and black cheek ruffs

entries.notes: A tree-climbing fox; the classic rabbit-behind-the-rabbit of the Southeast.

entries.name: Striped skunk
behaviour: warns with handstands and tail-raising before spraying up to 6 m
the great horned owl is nearly immune to the spray - its main predator
digs its own den but often inherits burrows from other animals

voxel_model.pattern: shiny black with a bold white dorsal crest splitting into two shoulder stripes

entries.notes: Spray is the defensive jack-in-the-box; otherwise a harmless, chicken-pilfering neighbour.

entries.name: Mexican free-tailed bat
entries.migrates: seasonal: southern US to Mexico for winter
behaviour: Bracken Cave holds ~20 million bats - the largest mammal gathering on Earth
emerges at dusk in a ribbon miles long, vacuuming up migrating moths
swift, straight flight up to 100+ km/h at high altitude

voxel_model.pattern: dark chocolate-brown with long narrow wings and a protruding tail past the tail membrane

entries.notes: Bracken Cave near San Antonio, Texas is the must-see landmark; the evening emergence empties and refills the sky.

entries.name: Southern tamandua
behaviour: arboreal and terrestrial; rips bark off dead wood to reach ant and termite nests
prehensile tail lets it wrap its grip around branches and larvae tubes
hissing, sneezing aggression displays with raised forearms and urine droplets

voxel_model.pattern: golden tan with a bold black 'vest' band across the torso and back

entries.notes: The smaller, hairier, vested cousin of the giant anteater; follows ant trails with 30-second licks.

entries.name: Crab-eating fox
behaviour: despite the name, fruit is often the staple - palm and fig dominate many samples
hunts singly but forages afield of the burrow; males help provision lactating females
easily habituates around ranches and wet-season riverbanks

voxel_model.pattern: sandy-grizzled back with dark shoulders and a bushy black-tipped tail

entries.notes: Nowhere called 'crab' appropriately: a wide-ranging generalist of floodplains and gallery forest.

entries.name: Pygmy marmoset
behaviour: the world's smallest monkey - fits in a coat pocket, feeds on tree exudates
gouges bark with sap-tapping incisors and revisits wells on a schedule
family groups with a single breeding pair; older siblings help raise the twins

voxel_model.pattern: banded tawny-and-buff tail, big round rusty ear tufts and a bright face halo

entries.notes: A pocket-sized gum-tapper of Amazon gallery forest; trade and pet-grab habitat loss have deepened its risk.

entries.name: Golden lion tamarin
behaviour: mane of flame-orange fur frames a dark face; groups groom in wiggly social pools
conservation flagship: rescued from ~200 animals to over 3,700 in the wild
fast, loud alarm calls; fossicks under bark with a tap-and-probe rhythm

voxel_model.pattern: full glossy golden-orange mane framing a hairless black face

entries.notes: Conservation's poster child for the Atlantic Forest; reintroduction programs around Rio have worked.

entries.name: Margay
behaviour: the only cat that regularly hunts hanging from one paw by the ankles
serviceable climber: hind ankles rotate 180 degrees, ankles leap upside-down along branches
imitates the calls of prey such as young tamarins to summon them

voxel_model.pattern: rosetted coat like a small ocelot, oversized eyes for low light

entries.notes: The squirrel-cat of the canopy: ankle-hung pounces and monkey-call mimicry make it a legend of the forest.

entries.name: Grey-headed flying fox
entries.migrates: nomadic: follows flower and fruit waves along the east coast
behaviour: roosts in 'camps' of tens of thousands in riparian corridors - a loud, smelly dusk exodus
key pollinator and seed disperser; moves eucalypt and rainforest pollen for kilometres
wingspan ~1 m; one pup per year born in the spring camp

voxel_model.pattern: rusty-grey shoulders, silver-grey mantle and a dark fox-like head

entries.notes: Night corridors of pollen in SE Australia; colonies under pressure from camp destruction and heatwaves.

entries.name: Feathertail glider
behaviour: the smallest gliding mammal on Earth - lighter than a AA battery
glides 20-25 m with a frayed, feather-like tail as a rudder
nests communally in tree hollows and under bark flakes in eucalyptus woods

voxel_model.pattern: grey back, white belly, feather-like fringed tail tip

entries.notes: Flag-sized glider you will only notice at the bird bath at night; a prized captive micro-jewel.

entries.name: Dusky antechinus
behaviour: all males die of stress-induced organ failure in a marathon two-week mating season - semelparity at its most extreme
fierce hunters for their size - will take down prey nearly as big as themselves
nests communally in winter for warmth; females raise one litter

voxel_model.pattern: dark smoky-brown marsupial-mouse mask, pointed snout and long scaly tail

entries.notes: A firecracker of a marsupial mouse: one eruptive mating season, then every male is dead.

entries.name: Blue duiker
behaviour: the smallest antelope in mainland Africa - rarely leaves the undergrowth
freezes stock-still, then explodes through tangled stems at the first clap
midden latrines mark paths through forest understory

voxel_model.pattern: blue-grey sheen, straight short horns in males, white speckling on the rump

entries.notes: Forest antelope of Central and West African bush: a sneeze of adrenaline in two pounds and horns.

entries.name: Indian giant squirrel
behaviour: among the loudest morning chatterers in Satpura and the Western Ghats
leaps up to 6 m between trunks and frees fruit with a rotating wrist grip
nests of twigs and leaves in tall trees, used repeatedly but abandoned yearly

voxel_model.pattern: chocolate-and-cream head, maroon flanks, jet tail with a pale tip

entries.notes: State animal of Maharashtra; a Ghats icon and one of the easiest canopy mammals to spot on hikes.

entries.name: Asian palm civet
behaviour: kopi luwak raw material: swallows whole coffee cherries, passes the bean half-fermented
bold around towns - raided fruit stores, temples and residential rooftops
just as happy in dense jungle as in coconut plantations and persimmon groves

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with three dark stripes and dark spots down the back, banded face mask

entries.notes: The discreet bean-to-cup ingredient behind the world's most divisive coffee; a cheeky rooftop-dweller.

entries.name: Sunda slow loris
behaviour: the only venomous primate: licks brachial-gland oil into a saliva cocktail that bites sting for months
moves at deliberate loris pace - three limbs always on the support
huge round eyes for low light; no tail to speak of

voxel_model.pattern: caramel coat, white face with a dark teardrop eye-stripe and a dorsal midline stripe

entries.notes: Photogenic 'staring' loris of the pet trade; their huge eyes hide a genuine venom gland.

entries.name: Ruby-throated hummingbird
entries.migrates: trans-Gulf: eastern US to Mexico and Central America in autumn
behaviour: crosses the Gulf of Mexico in one 500-mile overnight flight, doubling its body weight on nectar
figure-eight wing beats beat ~53 times per second - hovering without will
males court with a steep U-shaped dive that whines with tail-feathers

voxel_model.pattern: emerald back, white throat, gorget of metallic ruby-red in males

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. The jewel of the eastern feeder; a single fly-over-the-Gulf marvel.

entries.name: Northern cardinal
behaviour: males are scarlet with black face masks; females are the buff-brown bettors singing back
sings year-round, including mid-winter thaws and warm evenings
prefers dense shrub thickets and hedgerows for nesting

voxel_model.pattern: all-over scarlet male with black mask; crested silhouette; buff-brown singing female

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. The everyday flagship of the North American feeder; state bird of seven states.

entries.name: Eastern screech owl
behaviour: two colour morphs - red and grey - same species, no geography split
haunting descending whinny and tremolo trill carry across swamp woods
cavities only: abandoned woodpecker holes, nest boxes and even old mailboxes

voxel_model.pattern: small ear tufts, mottled bark-camouflage, two morphs so grey vs rufous both fine

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. Finger-sized owl of the eastern hollow tree; the classic night-keeper call.

entries.name: Toco toucan
entries.migrates: local: moves between fruiting trees in flocks
behaviour: bill is 30-50% of body surface area; filled with air pockets, light as a feather, works as a thermal radiator
keystone seed disperser of the gallery forest; raids eagle nests and steals hyacinth-macaw eggs
grunting, croaking chorus fills the cerrado dawn

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black body, white bib, enormous yellow-orange bill with a black oval spot

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. Brazil's bird-of-Rio icon and the biggest of all toucans; a frugivore engineer.

entries.name: Amazonian motmot
behaviour: sits on a bare branch like a judge; tail rackets swing like a metronome when a predator passes
buries no-poisonous prey alive in clay to detoxify before eating
burrows its own nest hole in clay banks

voxel_model.pattern: teal-blue body, chestnut back, black mask outlined in turquoise, racket-tipped tail

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. The watchful kingfisher cousin with the swinging racket tail of the Amazon.

entries.name: Superb fairywren
behaviour: males turn cobalt-blue only in breeding season - otherwise moult back to brown
cooperative family units: older siblings feed new chicks
famous scuttling hop through leaf litter, cocking its tail over its back

voxel_model.pattern: sapphire-blue crown, ear patches and shoulders in season; long cocked tail

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. Australia's blue jewel of the shrub thicket; a favourite garden muse.

entries.name: Australian magpie
behaviour: duels rival groups and dive-bombs joggers in a swooping spring 'magpie season'
carolling dawn chorus from the highest gum - deadliest siren in the suburbs
builds big messy stick-nests above 10 m; very smart, often learns picnic routines

voxel_model.pattern: black head and wings with white mantle and nape flash, long wedge tail

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. National bird in waiting; spring swooper of the Australian oval.

entries.name: Chinese hwamei
behaviour: immortalised in Chinese lore as the 'hundred-song bird' - a world-class mimicking singer
haunted bamboo groves of Fujian; singing contests judged on duration, variety and purity
nervous, secretive skulker; flicking sideways hops through scrub

voxel_model.pattern: dark eyebrow bordered white, streaked brown back, bold white-striped throat, long tail

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. China's most celebrated cage-songbird; a fierce, brilliant garden mimic.

entries.name: Red junglefowl
behaviour: the wild ancestor of every chicken on Earth - domesticated ~8,000 years ago
roosters crow at dawn from a high roost; hens lead chick lines through leaf litter
roosts in trees at night, runs fast in bursts, flushes rarely

voxel_model.pattern: fiery comb and wattles, iridescent green-gold hackle, rust-red saddle back

entries.notes: gestation_days is incubation time. Wild chicken of the Asian jungle; company for curious road-dwellers.

entries.name: Eastern hognose snake
behaviour: bluffs violently - spreads neck, hisses, strikes with a closed mouth - then plays dead with tongue out and belly up
immune to toad toxins; nose is a shovel for digging in loose sand
harmless to humans despite the theatrics

voxel_model.pattern: upturned shovel snout, blotched sandy-brown, black V-shaped head marking

entries.notes: gestation_days is egg incubation time. The drama queen of the Southeast: all bluff, no bite, dead as doornails when cornered.

entries.name: Five-lined skink
behaviour: hatchlings have electric-blue tails that detach on purpose - a bright decoy for predators
females guard egg clutches in damp logs; very fast and shiny on hot days
adult males grow orange chins and lose the stripes with age

voxel_model.pattern: juvenile electric-blue tail, five pale longitudinal stripes, shiny black head

entries.notes: gestation_days is egg incubation time. The blue-tailed glitter of every warm log and dry stone wall east of the Mississippi.

entries.name: Eastern blue-tongued skink
behaviour: waddles like a bear and flashes a cobalt-blue tongue at anything that startles it
live-bearer: mother gestates miniature skinks for about four months
late riser: hates cold mornings, puffs up, wheezes, and plays statue

voxel_model.pattern: stout striped body in russet and grey, cobalt-blue tongue when threatened

entries.notes: gestation_days is null: it bears live young. Australia's favourite pet lizard - tolerant of hands, snail-powered menace to gardens.

entries.name: Tokay gecko
behaviour: the shouted 'to-kay, to-kay' repeat gives it its name - a wall-bouncing 0.4 m shout
adhesive toe-pads climb glass; bites hard and hangs on with a bone-crushing grip
nests in wall crevices and behind temple statues; feeds on geckos smaller than itself

voxel_model.pattern: blue-grey base with orange-red spots, huge golden-eyed stare

entries.notes: gestation_days is egg incubation time. The household guardian of Southeast Asia; a shouting, spotted rat-catcher.

entries.name: American toad
behaviour: 1-4 weeks of inflated trills at every vernal pool in spring - one male can out-sing 200 others
winter-digs below frost line; chemical defense: bufotoxin from parotoid glands
walks rather than hops; gardeners' friend, eating thousands of pests

voxel_model.pattern: warty tan back with dark spots, kidney-shaped parotoid glands behind the eyes

entries.notes: The warty night toad behind the garden watering hole; trilling choruses define the first warm rain of April.

entries.name: Eastern newt
behaviour: three life acts: aquatic larva, bright-orange 'red eft' on land for 3-7 years, then olive aquatic adult
tetrodotoxin in skin makes the red eft nearly bite-proof to birds and frogs
returns to the same pond year after year for breeding

voxel_model.pattern: vermilion 'red eft' stage with black-ringed orange spots; olive aquatic adult

entries.notes: A walking orange emergency: the eft's skin toxin is the same family as pufferfish poison.

entries.name: American green treefrog
behaviour: southern belle of the porch light - snags moths one snap at a time
hollow palm tree-huggers: ordinary suburban yards host whole colonies
peeps like a duck-billed banjo during warm southern nights

voxel_model.pattern: lime-green body, creamy-white side stripe from jaw to groin

entries.notes: The classic frog on the window screen; an easy, musical indicator that the yard still breathes.

entries.name: Big dipper firefly
behaviour: J-shaped hook dance at dusk - males flash in synchrony during warm humid weeks
larvae hunt slugs and snails in soil; adults live days and flash to find mates
firefly numbers are crashing under lawn and light pollution

voxel_model.pattern: dark elytra with a yellow-green lightning belly

entries.notes: The lightning bugs of childhood summers; the J-hook flash is the silhouette of American June nights.

entries.name: Giant honeybee
entries.migrates: seasonal: migrates between flower waves at altitude
behaviour: nests in single huge open combs hanging from cliff faces and high branches - the 'mad honey' bee
dances with a shimmering wave across the comb curtain when disturbed
produces red honey coveted in the hills of Nepal

voxel_model.pattern: large orange-and-black striped bee on an open curtain comb

entries.notes: The Himalayan rock-cliff dweller whose red mad honey is still harvested by ladder-dropping gurungs.

entries.name: Harlequin beetle
behaviour: males have forelegs longer than their body - used like jousting lances at sap flows
flies to dead and dying trees miles away; hosts a whole phoretic pseudoscorpion army under its wings
head-body 4.3-7.5 cm; the giant of the Neotropical longhorn beetles

voxel_model.pattern: black-orange-green harlequin pattern, absurdly long male forelegs

entries.notes: The supermodel of the beetle world: collectors' grail, pseudoscorpion ferryman, and pheromone knight of the fallen tree.

entries.name: Redback spider
behaviour: close relative of the black widow; females sport a broad crimson dorsal band
males voluntarily offer themselves as the sexual afterglow snack - a famous suicide mating ritual
the second-most-feared Australian bite behind the funnel-web

voxel_model.pattern: shiny jet black with one thick red dorsal stripe

entries.notes: gestation_days is egg-sac incubation time. Likes sheds, toilet seats and old tyres - Australia's commonest venomous worry.

entries.name: Largemouth bass
behaviour: the bass of every American pond poster - giant mouth extends past the eye
ambush predator of lily pads and fallen timber; explosive strike within range of shade
rowdy males guard nests in shallow water - notorious in catch-and-release season

voxel_model.pattern: dark olive back, white belly, broad lateral blotches; huge hinged mouth

entries.notes: The apex pond-bully of warm American water; an invasive export reshaping warm fisheries worldwide.

entries.name: Japanese medaka
behaviour: staple paddy-rice field fish for centuries; now a lab darling for genetics and behaviour
glow-in-the-dark variants sold as 'gloFish' descend from medaka in Japan and US
schools in shallow ponds and flooded rice paddies, darting under duckweed

voxel_model.pattern: translucent silvery-gold with faint orange flanks; males carry broader anal fins

entries.notes: Little rice-paddy fish with outsized fame: a model organism, a first aquarium fish, and a pest-control ally.

entries.name: Giant African land snail
behaviour: a fist-sized snail that lays up to 2,500 eggs a year - among the world's worst invasive species
eats stucco off houses for calcium; chews through over 500 kinds of plants
Miami and Florida keep losing ground to it despite constant eradication campaigns

voxel_model.pattern: conical streaked shell in tan and brown bands; long body with horn-like rhinophores

entries.notes: A slug-like invasion in a shell; one of the most-eradicated snails on Earth - and still munching your garden.

entries.name: Red swamp crayfish
behaviour: bulldozes rice-paddy tunnels in Louisiana - the crawfish behind every boil
highly adaptable invader; out-competes natives on nearly every continent
walks backwards with a flicked tail in a flash of crimson

voxel_model.pattern: deep crimson shell with darker mottling; big crusher claws

entries.notes: The crawfish of New Orleans and every backyard boil; an ecological wrecking ball elsewhere on Earth.
